newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds scoot ahead, spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds scoot ahead, spreads tighten.

text.p: Light buying bolstered the prices of U.S. mortgage-backed securities in late trade on Wednesday, mortgage experts said.
Pass-through yield spreads narrowed to Treasuries by a fraction, helped by a dip in the Treasury market earlier in the day and lack of supply from mortgage bankers.
Mortgage traders said that fixed-rate discount coupons were the flavor of the day.
"We bought some discounts today which is pretty unusual for us," said one head Ginnie trader. He said his firm scooped up 6.5 and 7.0 percent, 15-year and 30-year Ginnie paper.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was up 16/32 at 99-09/32, yielding 90 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 16/32 higher as well, at 99-13/32 and 99-16/32, respectively.
Five-year Treasuries were up 9/32 at 6.57 percent, and 10-year notes were up 13/32 at 6.76 percent.
Earlier in the day, the Commerce Department reported that Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew 5.6 percent in the first quarter, a higher number than the market had expected.
